analysis:
Both changed files are test code under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. No production source, key handling, attestation, coordinator WebSocket, cache crypto or authorization paths change.

SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift (head lines 45-48) changes the gpt-oss-20b fixture dtypes from [bf16] + 23x fp32 to 24x bf16. The comment says the SDK's expert SwiGLU now keeps the bf16 activation dtype, so every layer stores bf16 K/V. This only alters the test-side AdmissionV2 layerElementBytes and PagedKVPoolConfig layerDTypes inputs. It is configuration-only and involves no weights or tensors.

EngineV2PrefixCacheWiringTests.swift (head lines 435-436 and 445) changes comments only. The assertions are unchanged: the fallback contiguous GPT-OSS delta is still nominal + 2048.

Threat relevance is indirect. Resource accounting touches T-041 and T-010/T-029 availability, since KV sizing feeds admission and heartbeat token budgets. The fixture change implies production sizing may now be less conservative for gpt-oss, because bf16 K/V halves the per-token bytes versus fp32. This is a correctness and availability concern, not a confidentiality one.

The production side of this (EngineV2Factory, AdmissionV2, SDK activation dtype) is not in the supplied evidence. If the claim that the SDK now keeps bf16 is wrong, KV under-reservation could cause over-admission and memory pressure. The production fallback in slotKVBytesPerToken when native types are not observed remains conservative fp32 per the retained test at lines 437-443. This needs verification by a reviewer who sees the production diff, but I identified no concrete security regression here.

No new attack surface, secret exposure, or invalidated threat-model assumption is introduced by these test changes.
